item.title: #3620645: Guzzle FW Gadget Chain shim followup
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +310/−3 · php +305 · lock +3/−2 · json +2/−1
  • Diff: 6379cc8
  • Discussion: #3620645 · 3 contributors · 15 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 3 contributors

Summary

This is a backport of the fix from #3524971, which hardens Guzzle's FileCookieJar class against a known PHP object-injection "gadget chain" that could let an attacker who controls unserialized data force an arbitrary file write. That protection had only landed on the 11.x development branch; this issue brings the same shim to the 10.6.x, 11.3.x, and 11.4.x release branches, so sites running those core versions get the defense too. It also fixes a deprecation warning in the shim code that had already been committed to 11.x.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: The hardened \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar shim that defends against a PHP object-injection file-write gadget chain (see #3524971) is now also shipped on the 10.6.x, 11.3.x, and 11.4.x branches, not just 11.x.

Technical details

The fix adds core/includes/guzzle_file_cookie_jar_shim.php to the 10.6.x, 11.3.x, and 11.4.x branches, registered via each branch's composer.json/composer.lock autoload files list alongside includes/bootstrap.inc. The shim conditionally defines \GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar (only if the real Guzzle class hasn't already loaded) as a verbatim backport of the hardened Guzzle 8.0 implementation: it adds a private $autoSave flag that __wakeup() sets to false, so an instance reconstructed from attacker-controlled serialized data no longer triggers a file write in __destruct().

On all four branches (including 11.x, where the shim already existed), save() and load() were changed to call PHP's native json_encode()/json_decode() with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR instead of GuzzleHttp\Utils::jsonEncode()/jsonDecode(). Those Utils methods are deprecated as of guzzlehttp/guzzle 7.15 and removed in 8.0; the deprecation only surfaced once Guzzle was upgraded past the version core had previously been pinned to (7.12.1). Each branch also got a corresponding FileCookieJarShimTest in core/tests/Drupal/Tests/Component/Cookie/, adapted to each branch's PHPUnit annotation style (@group vs. the #[Group] attribute).</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 3, 2026
  • Committed: September 11, 2026 (8 days and 4 commits later)

  • mcdruid (Acquia)

Collaboration

mcdruid tracked down why the deprecation only appeared now: guzzle is normally pinned to 7.12.1, which predates the GuzzleHttp\Utils::jsonEncode()/jsonDecode() deprecation introduced in 7.15, so it wasn't caught until the backport exercised a newer Guzzle.

item.title: #2638250: The label "Member for" on user profiles is hardcoded markup that is different from other user fields
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 22 files, +256/−31 · php +241/−16 · yml +15/−15
  • Diff: 429cf50
  • Discussion: #2638250 · 24 contributors · 115 comments
  • Followers: 35
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 24 contributors

Summary

The "Member for" text on user profile pages used to be hard-coded HTML markup (a <h4> element) baked into user.module, which meant it could not be restyled, wasn't overridable via normal field templates, had accessibility issues, and had a cache-invalidation bug because its time interval wasn't captured as cache metadata. Drupal now exposes the user entity's existing created field as a normal, configurable field on the "Manage display" page (hidden by default), and deprecates the old member_for extra field, scheduled for removal in Drupal 13. Sites that currently show "Member for" will keep showing it after upgrading to 11.5 or 12 (nothing changes visually), but a deprecation notice will appear whenever it renders, prompting site owners to switch their display configuration to the created field, which behaves like any other field and can be labeled, formatted, and themed normally. New installations have both fields hidden by default.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: The user entity's created field is now configurable on the user "Manage display" page (hidden by default); a post-update hook adds it as hidden to existing user displays.
  • Deprecation: The member_for user profile extra field is deprecated as of Drupal 11.5 and will be removed in Drupal 13; use the created field instead.

Technical details

In User::baseFieldDefinitions(), the created base field gained ->setDisplayOptions('view', ['region' => 'hidden'])->setDisplayConfigurable('view', TRUE), so it now appears on the user "Manage display" screen like any other field instead of being invisible to Field UI. UserHooks::entityExtraFieldInfo() relabels member_for to "Member for (deprecated)" and sets 'visible' => FALSE in its hook_entity_extra_field_info() definition. UserHooks::userView() still builds the same hard-coded <h4 class="label"> render array for backward compatibility, but now wraps it in a #post_render callback, triggerMemberForDeprecation(), which raises an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice referencing the change record at https://www.drupal.org/node/3611943.

A new post-update function, user_post_update_add_created_to_display(), uses ConfigEntityUpdater to add created to the hidden section of every user entity view display that doesn't already define it, so upgrading sites gain the new field definition without any visible change. Default install profile displays (core.entity_view_display.user.user.*) now list both created and member_for under hidden and no longer include member_for under content. Drupal\user\UserListBuilder, used by the admin /admin/people listing, renamed its "Member for" table column key from member_for to created to match.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Sites and contrib/custom code that reference the member_for extra field (for example in EntityViewDisplay configuration, or custom code checking $display->getComponent('member_for')) should switch to the created field instead, since member_for is deprecated in Drupal 11.5 and will be removed in Drupal 13:

// Old: relied on the always-visible, hard-coded 'member_for' extra field.

// New: enable the 'created' base field on the user display, e.g. via
// Manage Display UI, or programmatically:
EntityViewDisplay::collectRenderDisplay($user, 'default')
  ->setComponent('created', [
    'type' => 'timestamp_ago', // or 'timestamp', etc.
  ])
  ->save();

Code that keys off the /admin/people listing's "Member for" column by machine name should use created instead of member_for (see Drupal\user\UserListBuilder::buildHeader()/buildRow()).

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 20, 2015
  • First commit: September 4, 2026 (10 years later)
  • Last commit: September 11, 2026 (6 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • vladimiraus (Technocrat)
  • markhalliwell (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • adamps (AlbanyWeb)
  • xjm (Acquia)
  • geerlingguy (Acquia)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • mohit_aghera (PreviousNext)
  • medha kumari (Dotsquares Ltd.)
  • jayelless
  • kentr
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • godotislate

Collaboration

This issue was open for nearly a decade with several competing proposals. Berdir (#comment ~14508451) pushed back on an earlier "convert to a computed field" approach as unnecessarily complex, arguing the display's only real job was showing created with a different label, and suggested instead making created configurable with an overridable label; larowlan agreed this was the better path. Years later godotislate picked up the implementation, initially tried rendering created with the TimestampFormatter's JS-driven time-diff display, but ran into cache-invalidation test failures (DateFormatter::formatDiff() cacheability has max-age 0) and needed help from berdir and catch on Slack to fix the performance tests. After that proved complex, godotislate switched to the simpler "hide created by default" approach berdir and larowlan had originally proposed, which Gábor Hojtsy confirmed as acceptable on Slack before it was committed.

item.title: #3391683: Convert initial functions in update.inc file to a class
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +327/−159 · php +324/−159 · yml +3
  • Diff: 5ac5b9c
  • Discussion: #3391683 · 11 contributors · 42 comments
  • Followers: 13
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 11 contributors

Summary

Drupal core has deprecated several procedural functions from the update.inc include file: update_check_requirements(), update_system_schema_requirements(), update_do_one(), and the internal _update_fix_missing_schema(). Their logic has moved to a new Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate service class. This is part of a longer-running effort to stop relying on manually included legacy .inc files and let the class autoloader handle this code instead. There is no behavioral change for site owners; this only affects developers and contrib/custom code that calls these functions directly.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: update_check_requirements(), update_system_schema_requirements(), update_do_one(), and _update_fix_missing_schema() in update.inc are deprecated in favor of methods on the new Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate service.
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate autowired service providing getRequirements(), systemSchemaRequirements(), and doOne().

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate class (registered as an autowired service) exposes getRequirements(), systemSchemaRequirements(), doOne(), and an @internal fixMissingSchema() method, reproducing the logic that used to live in the standalone functions but using constructor-injected dependencies (UpdateHookRegistry, ModuleHandlerInterface, MessengerInterface, LoggerChannelFactoryInterface) instead of \Drupal::service() lookups. The old update.inc functions are now thin deprecated wrappers that trigger E_USER_DEPRECATED and delegate to \Drupal::service(DatabaseUpdate::class).

DbUpdateController was updated to take DatabaseUpdate and UpdateHookRegistry as (nullable, for backward-compatible construction) constructor arguments, using them internally instead of calling update_check_requirements() or \Drupal::service('update.update_hook_registry') directly. The batch operation that used to invoke the procedural update_do_one callback now calls the class method callable DatabaseUpdate::class . ':doOne'. This issue was scoped to the first three functions of update.inc; it is a followup to the "#2999721: [META] Deprecate the legacy include files before Drupal 9" effort, and further update.inc functions are handled in separate follow-up issues.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to the deprecated update.inc functions with the new service:

// Before:
$requirements = update_check_requirements();
$schema_requirements = update_system_schema_requirements();
update_do_one($module, $number, $dependency_map, $context);

// After:
$requirements = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate::class)->getRequirements();
$schema_requirements = \Drupal::service(\Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate::class)->systemSchemaRequirements();
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\Core\Update\DatabaseUpdate::class)->doOne($module, (int) $number, $dependency_map, $context);

_update_fix_missing_schema() has no direct public replacement; its logic is now DatabaseUpdate::fixMissingSchema(), which is marked @internal.

Any code constructing DbUpdateController directly should pass the new $databaseUpdate and $updateHookRegistry constructor arguments; omitting them still works but triggers a deprecation notice and will be required in Drupal 13.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 4, 2023
  • Committed: September 11, 2026 (2 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • xjm (HeroDevs)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)

  • mradcliffe (Kosada)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • dcam
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • amateescu

Collaboration

This issue sat dormant for a long time after initial review from xjm and larowlan before mradcliffe picked it up, rebased it repeatedly through several conflicting core changes (including #3303751 and #3561302), and iterated through multiple rounds of review feedback from nicxvan, dcam, kim.pepper, and amateescu, including a design discussion about whether to use ClassResolver versus \Drupal::service() for the new service (resolved in favor of ::service() per nicxvan's comment) and whether doOne() should be static (resolved as a protected instance method per larowlan's earlier review).

item.title: #3035343: Deprecate drupal_attach_tabledrag(). Move its logic in Table form element
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +231/−153 · php +226/−152 · js +4/−1 · txt +1
  • Diff: 770e6f0
  • Discussion: #3035343 · 15 contributors · 98 comments
  • Followers: 23
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 15 contributors

Summary

Drupal has long supported "tabledrag": draggable table rows used for reordering things like block regions, menu items, or field weights. The logic that wires this behavior to a table (previously the procedural drupal_attach_tabledrag() function) has been moved into the Table form element as a proper static method, and the old function is now deprecated. This is part of the ongoing effort to remove procedural code from common.inc. Site builders and users won't notice any functional difference; draggable tables continue to work exactly as before. Module developers who called drupal_attach_tabledrag() directly (for example, custom admin tables with reorderable rows) should switch to the new method ahead of Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Tables using #tabledrag now render with an added tabledrag-enabled class and a data-drupal-tabledrag attribute; the JS no longer relies solely on the table's id.
  • Deprecation: drupal_attach_tabledrag() is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0; use \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\Table::attachTabledrag() instead.
  • New API: New public static method \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\Table::attachTabledrag() contains the logic formerly in drupal_attach_tabledrag().

Technical details

The function body of drupal_attach_tabledrag() in core/includes/common.inc was moved verbatim into a new public static method, \Drupal\Core\Render\Element\Table::attachTabledrag(), and the original function now just triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED error and delegates to it. All core callers (Table::preRenderTable(), FieldUiTable::tablePreRender(), and the Views UI rearrange-filter form) were updated to call the new method directly.

As part of the move, the internal counter used to generate a unique tabledrag instance ID per table (previously stored via drupal_static()) was reworked twice during the issue's long history: first to a static class property, then, after concerns raised about correctness in the memory cache and long-running PHP contexts, to \Drupal::cache('memory') keyed by Table::TABLE_DRAG_CACHE_ID, so the counter doesn't get reset unexpectedly between requests handled by the same PHP process (e.g. FrankenPHP, RoadRunner). The table's HTML id is still printed for backward compatibility, but the internal selector used to wire up the JS behavior was switched from the raw id to a dedicated data-drupal-tabledrag attribute (plus a tabledrag-enabled class), and core/misc/tabledrag.js's once() selector was updated to match on [data-drupal-tabledrag="${base}"] instead of #${base}.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: February 24, 2019
  • Committed: September 11, 2026 (7 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • andypost (Skilld)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • finnsky (Skilld)
  • voleger (Drupal Ukraine Community)
  • naresh_bavaskar (QED42)
  • nod_ (Smile)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • daffie
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • claudiu.cristea (Webikon)
  • kim.pepper (PreviousNext)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)

Collaboration

This issue took over six years to land because of a substantive, recurring technical debate. Early on, claudiu.cristea and andypost argued over whether the new method should be called via self:: or static:: so subclasses could override just attachTabledrag() without duplicating preRenderTable(); claudiu.cristea's late-static-binding explanation (with a 3v4l.org example) settled it in favor of allowing proper overriding.

catch then pointed out that relying on an incrementing counter tied to a table's HTML id is unsafe with dynamic page cache, since two independently-cached blocks rendered in different requests could collide on the same ID, and proposed switching to a data-* attribute (issue #1090592 territory). nod_ significantly simplified the resulting JS patch, showing that only the once() selector needed to change, without new CSS classes or state-tracking. alexpott later caught a subtle off-by-one regression in the counter refactor (starting at 1 instead of 0) introduced by the static-property rewrite. Years later, catch re-raised the original concern that a static property still didn't solve the multi-request collision problem, and nicxvan and catch worked out the eventual fix: storing the counter in the memory cache bin instead of a static property.

item.title: #3618971: Use Admin theme in installer
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +167/−36 · php +167/−36
  • Diff: 865fea9
  • Discussion: #3618971 · 11 contributors · 59 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 11 contributors

Summary

The installer, update.php, and any early maintenance-mode pages (shown when the database or bootstrap is unavailable) now use the Admin theme (default_admin) instead of Claro. This is a step toward deprecating Claro. Distribution profiles that need a different installer theme can still request one via the distribution.install.theme key in their info file, and sites can still override the theme by setting $settings['maintenance_theme'] in settings.php.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: The maintenance_theme example in default.settings.php now shows default_admin instead of claro; sites that explicitly set $settings['maintenance_theme'] = 'claro'; keep working, but the out of the box default for install, update.php and early maintenance pages is now default_admin.
  • New API: New \Drupal\Core\Installer\InstallerKernel::INSTALL_THEME constant identifies the theme used for install, update, and early maintenance pages, replacing hardcoded 'claro' strings throughout core.

Technical details

The hardcoded 'claro' fallback used in install_state_defaults(), _drupal_maintenance_theme(), and InstallerKernel::getExtensions() was replaced with a new InstallerKernel::INSTALL_THEME constant ('default_admin'). InstallerKernel::getExtensions() was refactored into a new private getInstallThemes() helper that resolves the install theme (and its base themes, unless the theme is the default install theme, which declares base theme: false so no filesystem scan is needed) whether or not a profile has been selected yet.

A new InstallerKernel::updateThemes() override keeps the install theme's hook implementations registered throughout the whole install process: normally, installing a profile or recipe replaces the theme registry with just the themes the profile installed, which drops the install theme's hooks (Drupal\Core\Hook\ThemeHookCollectorPass) even though the install theme keeps rendering the remaining pages, including the final "configure site" step. This previously caused subtle breakage such as fonts not being preloaded and custom installer-theme hook implementations disappearing mid-install; both are now covered by new assertions in InstallerTest and test_installer_theme.

Other fixes needed to make default_admin usable during install: HtmlResponseAttachmentsProcessor::processAttachments() now uses $this->fileUrlGenerator->generateString() for preloaded fonts so the URL is root-relative instead of relative to install.php; default_admin's PreprocessHooks::preprocessHtml() now short-circuits toolbar/navigation class handling via InstallerKernel::installationAttempted() because permission checks need a database that does not exist yet during install; and default_admin\Settings::getAdminTheme() now returns ?string (falling back to the active theme) since system.theme configuration is unavailable during install.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: August 25, 2026
  • First commit: September 10, 2026 (15 days later)
  • Last commit: September 11, 2026 (1 day and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • jurgenhaas (LakeDrops)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)
  • mherchel (Dripyard)
  • godotislate
  • daffie (Finalist)
  • xjm (Zoocha)

Collaboration

Several contributors manually re-tested the installer end to end as the MR evolved and turned up real regressions rather than cosmetic issues: mherchel found the requirements/status-report styling was broken by an incorrect .root CSS selector (instead of :root) in the admin theme's variables and split that into #3619253 so it could be fixed and backported quickly; jurgenhaas and quietone both hit a 404/PluginNotFoundException after completing install, which took several rounds of independent reproduction attempts (including ruling out contrib modules and ECA) before daffie, disclosing use of AI to find the fix, resolved the "site install functionality" breakage. godotislate's later review caught that the 11.x backport had missed removing the obsolete test_installer_theme.theme file from an earlier unrelated cleanup (#3579903), which quietone corrected before the backport landed. xjm documented, for posterity, that she had previously opposed committing this ahead of the Admin theme reaching stable, but agreed to allow it for the installer only (not for backporting to stable branches) to unblock the broader Claro deprecation effort.

item.title: #3182064: Allow min & max exposed numeric/date filters to be configured
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +388/−6 · php +202/−6 · yml +186
  • Diff: c6e7444
  • Discussion: #3182064 · 17 contributors · 57 comments
  • Followers: 21
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 17 contributors

Summary

Exposed numeric and date range filters (the "between" operator, showing two input fields) previously always labeled their fields "Min" and "Max", which made little sense for a date range like "Authored on". Views now lets you configure these labels per filter, under "Minimum value label" and "Maximum value label" in the exposed filter settings. New filters default to "Minimum"/"Maximum" for numeric fields and "Start date"/"End date" for date fields; existing exposed filters keep showing "Min"/"Max" after upgrade so nothing changes visually unless you opt in.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Views numeric filter expose config gains min_label and max_label keys (defaults Minimum/Maximum, or Start date/End date for date filters); views_post_update_filter_min_max_labels() back-fills existing exposed filters with the legacy Min/Max labels so upgrading sites keep their current display.

Technical details

The change lives in NumericFilter and the date filter that extends it (views.filter.numeric/date schema in views.schema.yml). defineOptions() and defaultExposeOptions() add min_label/max_label to the expose array, and buildExposeForm() adds the two textfields (visible only when a two-value operator like "between" is selected, via the same #states used for the placeholder fields). valueForm() now sets $form['value']['min']['#title']/['max']['#title'] from $this->options['expose']['min_label']/max_label instead of the hardcoded t('Min')/t('Max').

Because this adds new config keys, ViewsConfigUpdater::needsMinMaxLabelUpdate()/processMinMaxLabelUpdate() and the views_post_update_filter_min_max_labels() post-update hook detect filters that already have min_placeholder (i.e. derive from NumericFilter) but lack min_label, and set both to the literal string Min/Max so upgraded sites render exactly as before. New views created after this change get the friendlier defaults instead.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: November 12, 2020
  • Committed: September 11, 2026 (5 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • pameeela
  • sophiavs (CI&T)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • ranjith_kumar_k_u (Material)

  • scott_euser (Soapbox)
  • dcam
  • xjm (Zoocha)

Collaboration

Reviewer dcam flagged that "Min" and "Max" are poor, likely-inaccessible abbreviations for the default labels, and suggested a follow-up to reconsider them. Views maintainer xjm agreed the defaults themselves needed improvement rather than just being configurable, and specifically proposed shipping "Start date"/"End date" as the date filter defaults; scott_euser then updated the implementation to use "Minimum"/"Maximum" and "Start date"/"End date" as the shipped defaults instead of the originally patched "Min"/"Max", while preserving the old abbreviated labels for existing sites via the update path.

item.title: #3620812: Move toolbar support from Workspaces to Toolbar
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +30/−23 · php +15/−10 · yml +13/−11 · css +2/−2
  • Diff: 0465fa0
  • Discussion: #3620812 · 8 contributors · 26 comments
  • Followers: 9
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 8 contributors

Summary

Sites that use the core Toolbar module together with Workspaces continue to see the workspace switcher tab in the toolbar exactly as before. This is an internal reorganization: the code that renders that tab now lives in the Toolbar module instead of the Workspaces UI module, but no toolbar behavior changes for site owners.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Previously, workspaces_ui owned a workspaces_ui.lazy_builders service (WorkspacesUiLazyBuilders) and a drupal.workspaces_ui.toolbar library that toolbar's ToolbarHooks::workspacesUiToolbar() depended on via #lazy_builder and an attached library, creating a dependency in the "wrong" direction (a UI module reaching into toolbar internals). This commit relocates that class into Drupal\toolbar as WorkspacesUiToolbarLinkBuilder, registered as toolbar.workspaces_ui_link_builder in toolbar.services.yml, and moves its CSS into a new toolbar.workspaces_ui library in toolbar.libraries.yml (the old drupal.workspaces_ui.toolbar library and its CSS are removed from workspaces_ui).

The initial patch simply deleted the toolbar integration from workspaces_ui, but reviewers longwave and larowlan objected that sites already using Toolbar (rather than the newer Navigation module) would silently lose the workspaces tab on upgrade, since Toolbar was still the default for many 11.0-11.3 sites until Navigation stabilized in 11.4. The approach was changed to a move instead of a removal.

The new toolbar.workspaces_ui_link_builder service is always registered, but its WorkspaceManagerInterface constructor argument is optional (@?workspaces.manager), so the service is inert when Workspaces isn't installed. Similarly, NavigationServiceProvider now checks container.modules for workspaces_ui instead of checking for the now-removed workspaces_ui.lazy_builders service when conditionally registering navigation.workspaces_lazy_builders. The WorkspacesLazyBuilder used by Navigation is a separate, unrelated class from the one moved here.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 4, 2026
  • Committed: September 9, 2026 (5 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • amateescu
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

The initial patch removed workspaces support from Toolbar entirely, on the reasoning (stated by catch) that "people can move to navigation if they want all bells and whistles." gábor hojtsy initially agreed this was fine given prior scoping in #3618746. But longwave raised a concrete upgrade concern: sites still on Toolbar (common for anyone who adopted Drupal before Navigation left experimental status in 11.4) would lose the feature going from 11.4 to 11.5 with no equivalent in Toolbar. larowlan agreed, expecting the code to be moved into toolbar rather than dropped. gábor hojtsy then reworked the patch into a move (a net +30 lines across 11 files) instead of a removal. longwave further suggested always registering the lazy builder service rather than conditionally, to avoid extra complexity since an unused service is harmless; gábor hojtsy adopted a nullable-argument pattern for this, noting it differed from the existing conditional-registration pattern used by NavigationServiceProvider. amateescu confirmed the revised, move-based approach was "much more update friendly."

item.description:

Summary

Drupal's internal logic for picking which plural form of a translated string to show (for example "1 apple" versus "3 apples", or the more complex rules some languages like Polish use) has been reorganized, and the old procedural helper locale_get_plural() is now deprecated and will be removed in Drupal 13. There is no behavior change for site visitors or translators: plural translations render exactly as before. The change is part of the long-running effort to remove procedural functions from locale.module and stop Drupal Core code from depending directly on the optional Locale module. Sites and modules that call locale_get_plural() directly (rare, since it was never part of the public plural-translation API) need to stop doing so before Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: TranslationInterface gains a new method selectPluralForm(int|float $count, string $string, ?string $langcode = NULL): string; custom classes implementing the interface directly must add it.
  • Deprecation: The procedural locale_get_plural() function is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 for removal in drupal:13.0.0, with no direct replacement.

Technical details

The plural-index logic that lived in locale_get_plural() moved behind a new TranslationInterface::selectPluralForm() method. The base implementation in Drupal\Core\StringTranslation\TranslationManager only distinguishes singular from plural (always returning index 1 for any count other than 1); the real per-language formula lookup now lives in a new Drupal\locale\TranslationManager, which extends the core class and injects the existing PluralFormulaInterface (locale.plural.formula) service to replicate what locale_get_plural() used to compute via \Drupal::service('locale.plural.formula')->getFormula(). LocaleServiceProvider::alter() swaps the string_translation service's class to this new Drupal\locale\TranslationManager whenever the Locale module is enabled; core.services.yml switched the string_translation service definition from a fixed argument list to autowire: true so the extra constructor dependency resolves automatically.

PluralTranslatableMarkup::translateString() now calls getStringTranslation()->selectPluralForm() instead of branching on function_exists('locale_get_plural') and \Drupal::hasService('locale.plural.formula'), removing a hardcoded Core-to-Locale dependency noted in a long-standing @todo referencing this issue. Two smaller, verifiable side effects landed with the refactor: selectPluralForm() types $count as int|float, so a non-numeric count passed to formatPlural() now throws a TypeError instead of silently mis-selecting a form; and PluralTranslatableMarkup::getArguments() now lets an explicitly supplied @count argument override the displayed value while the real $count still drives plural-form selection.

Related cleanups in the same area are tracked in #1577902 (removing drupal_static() usage across core) and #1273968 (original formula-caching work in locale.module, referenced in review as prior art for the static caching that was ultimately dropped here after benchmarking showed no measurable performance gain).

Upgrade

There is no direct replacement for locale_get_plural(). Use the normal plural translation API instead of computing the index yourself:

// Before:
$index = locale_get_plural($count, $langcode);

// After: let the translation system render the correct plural form directly.
$markup = \Drupal::translation()->formatPlural($count, '@count item', '@count items', [], ['langcode' => $langcode]);

If you implement Drupal\Core\StringTranslation\TranslationInterface directly (rather than extending TranslationManager), add the new required method:

public function selectPluralForm(int|float $count, string $string, ?string $langcode = NULL): string {
  // ...
}

Summary

Drupal's user account cancellation logic (blocking, deleting, or reassigning content when a user account is cancelled) has moved out of loose procedural functions in user.module and into a new AccountCancellation service. The four old functions, user_cancel(), _user_cancel(), _user_cancel_session_regenerate(), and user_cancel_methods(), still work but now emit deprecation warnings and simply delegate to the new service. This is purely an internal reorganization: end users see no behavior change, but module maintainers who call these functions directly need to update their code before Drupal 13.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: user_cancel(), _user_cancel(), _user_cancel_session_regenerate(), and user_cancel_methods() are deprecated in favor of the new Drupal\user\AccountCancellation service (cancel(), cancelAccount(), regenerateSession(), cancelMethods()), removed in Drupal 13.0.0.
  • New API: New Drupal\user\AccountCancellation service consolidating user account cancellation logic (cancel() and cancelMethods() are the public entry points).

Technical details

The new Drupal\user\AccountCancellation service, registered in user.services.yml, exposes cancel(array $edit, int $uid, string $method) (replacing user_cancel()), cancelMethods() (replacing user_cancel_methods()), plus the batch callbacks cancelAccount() (replacing _user_cancel(), marked @internal) and regenerateSession() (replacing _user_cancel_session_regenerate(), marked @internal). The deprecated procedural functions now just call \Drupal::service(AccountCancellation::class) and trigger E_USER_DEPRECATED warnings.

// Before:
user_cancel($edit, $uid, $method);
user_cancel_methods();

// After:
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\user\AccountCancellation::class)->cancel($edit, $uid, $method);
\Drupal::service(\Drupal\user\AccountCancellation::class)->cancelMethods();

Summary

Drupal core now ships its own console command for installing modules and themes, ex:install (also invokable as exin, pm:install, pm:enable, enable, or en), part of the "CLI in Core" initiative (#3582246). Previously this required a contributed tool like Drush. The command accepts a comma-separated list of module or theme machine names, resolves and reports any dependencies that will be pulled in, checks installation requirements the same way the admin "Extend" page does, and asks for confirmation before installing dependencies that were not explicitly requested (bypassable with --yes/-y). A --dry-run option previews what would happen without making changes. On success it lists Help, Permissions, and Configure links for each installed extension, mirroring what a site builder sees after installing from the UI. Modules and themes cannot be mixed in a single invocation.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ModuleInstallerInterface::getModulesToInstall() and ThemeInstallerInterface::getThemesToInstall() methods return the dependency-resolved list of modules/themes that would be installed, without installing them.

Technical details

Summary

Drupal core's experimental "Default Admin" theme (successor to the Gin admin theme merge) shipped with several Twig template overrides that were never actually reachable: menu-region--top.html.twig, menu-region--middle.html.twig, and menu-region--bottom.html.twig had no matching theme hook to attach to and were removed. No core-only site (not running Group, Quick Node Clone, or Paragraphs) will notice any change.

Investigation (in comments) traced each template's theme hook registration. default_admin declares no hook_theme() of its own, and its hook_theme_registry_alter() only repoints the toolbar and menu__toolbar hooks at templates/navigation; the Navigation module's hook_theme() registers top_bar*, block__navigation, navigation_menu, navigation_content_top, and navigation__messages, none of which is a menu_region base hook. Both files were just one-line {% extends '@default_admin/page/page--node.html.twig' %} wrappers. item.title: #3561302: Register equivalent updates on site install
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +150/−24 · php +145/−24 · yml +5
  • Diff: 1ab223a
  • Discussion: #3561302 · 9 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 10
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 9 contributors

Summary

Drupal tracks "equivalent updates" so that a database update backported to an older, still-supported branch is recognized as equivalent to the update that originally shipped it in a newer branch, preventing confusing warnings or double-running of updates. Previously this registration only happened when the corresponding hook_update_N() actually ran through update.php, but hook_update_N() functions never run on a brand-new site install. That meant a site installed directly on the older version (e.g. 10.4) never got the equivalent update recorded, so it could later show incorrect "you are trying to go backwards" warnings once it was upgraded past the version containing the original update. This fix registers those equivalent updates during module installation too, so freshly installed sites behave the same as sites that arrived at that version through running updates.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Calling UpdateHookRegistry::markFutureUpdateEquivalent() without the new $module and $ran_update_number arguments is deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and will be required in drupal:13.0.0; the method is now @internal, use the #[MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent] attribute instead (see #3617733).
  • New API: New Drupal\Core\Update\Attribute\MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent PHP attribute for hook_update_N() functions, letting the update be registered as equivalent even when the function never runs (e.g. on a fresh site install).

Technical details

The mechanism is a new #[MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent(futureUpdateNumber, futureVersionString)] PHP attribute applied directly to a hook_update_N() function, replacing the old pattern of calling \Drupal::service('update.update_hook_registry')->markFutureUpdateEquivalent() from inside the update function body. Because attributes can be discovered by reflection without invoking the function, ModuleInstaller::doInstall() now loops through every available update number returned by updateRegistry->getAvailableUpdates($module) during install, reflects each {$module}_update_{$version} function with ReflectionFunction, and if it carries the attribute, calls markFutureUpdateEquivalent() on its behalf, wrapping the reflection/registration in a try/catch that logs via Error::logException(). The same reflection check was added to update_do_one() in update.inc so the attribute also drives registration when updates run through update.php (previously that path relied on the explicit service call still present in the update function body).

UpdateHookRegistry::markFutureUpdateEquivalent() gained two new parameters, $module and $ran_update_number, currently accepted only via func_get_args() (commented out in the signature) to avoid a hard API break; calling it the old way now triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and falls back to determineModuleAndVersion(). The method is documented @internal since the attribute is now the supported way to register these. Core's own system.install equivalent-update declarations and the equivalent_update_test fixture module were converted to use the attribute, and a new equivalent_update_test_attribute_install test module and testAttributeOnInstall() test verify the install-time registration path.

Upgrade

Replace direct calls to markFutureUpdateEquivalent() inside an update function body with the attribute:

use Drupal\Core\Update\Attribute\MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent;

#[MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent(11101, '11.1.1')]
function my_module_update_10400(): void {
  // The function can be no-op.
}

Calling \Drupal::service('update.update_hook_registry')->markFutureUpdateEquivalent(11101, '11.1.1') directly from inside the update function still works but is deprecated and will require the $module and $ran_update_number arguments in Drupal 13 (see #3617733 and the change record at drupal.org/node/3572245).

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 3, 2025
  • Committed: September 7, 2026 (9 months and 2 commits later)

  • xjm (Zoocha)
  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

godotislate's initial proposal to solve this with a pair of attributes (MarkFutureUpdateEquivalent/CheckEquivalentUpdate) was discussed against an alternative catch raised, hard-coding equivalent branch numbers directly in update.php and site install, as brought up by xjm in Slack, before the reflection-based attribute approach was pursued in the MR. After review, alexpott pushed for the direct-call convention to be deprecated and markFutureUpdateEquivalent() marked @internal since "there is no reason to call it" once the attribute exists, which godotislate implemented and followed up on by filing #3617733 to make the new $module/$ran_update_number parameters required in Drupal 13. quietone later made substantial edits to the change record, trimming it to focus on the change itself and the action sites need to take, after noting a good example communicates more than lengthy prose.

item.title: #2025089: Deprecate user_role_grant_permissions(), user_role_revoke_permissions() and user_role_change_permissions()
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev

Summary

Drupal has long had three procedural helper functions for adding, removing, or bulk-changing the permissions on a user role: user_role_grant_permissions(), user_role_revoke_permissions(), and user_role_change_permissions(). These are now deprecated in favor of equivalent methods directly on the role entity's RoleInterface. Core's own call sites (tests, filter.module, the permissions form, and several contrib-adjacent modules) have all been converted to the new object-oriented API. Sites and contributed modules that call the old functions will get a deprecation notice and must switch before Drupal 13, where the functions are removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: user_role_grant_permissions(), user_role_revoke_permissions() and user_role_change_permissions() are deprecated in favor of RoleInterface::grantPermissions(), RoleInterface::revokePermissions() and RoleInterface::changePermissions().
  • New API: RoleInterface gains grantPermissions(array $permissions), revokePermissions(array $permissions) and changePermissions(array $permissions) methods for bulk permission changes on a role entity.

Technical details

RoleInterface gains three new methods: grantPermissions(array $permissions): static, revokePermissions(array $permissions): static, and changePermissions(array $permissions): static. The existing singular grantPermission() and revokePermission() methods on Role are now thin wrappers that cast their argument to an array and delegate to the new plural methods, so no behavior changes there. changePermissions() (previously only a procedural function's logic) is now a first-class interface method: it filters the given associative array into permissions to grant versus revoke and calls the other two methods accordingly.

The three deprecated procedural functions in user.module now load the role with \Drupal::entityTypeManager()->getStorage('user_role')->loadOverrideFree($rid), call the corresponding new RoleInterface method, save, and emit an E_USER_DEPRECATED trigger_error. Call sites throughout core (comment, file, filter, image, media, node, responsive_image, system, taxonomy, user tests, and filter.module's FilterFormat::postSave() and the permissions form submit handler) were updated to the pattern Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->grantPermissions([...])->save() (or revokePermissions()/changePermissions()), replacing direct calls to the deprecated functions. See #3620216 for the loadOverrideFree()/loadMultipleOverrideFree() API this conversion depends on.

Upgrade

Replace calls to the deprecated procedural functions with the equivalent RoleInterface methods on a loaded role entity:

// Before:
user_role_grant_permissions($rid, ['administer nodes']);
user_role_revoke_permissions($rid, ['administer nodes']);
user_role_change_permissions($rid, ['administer nodes' => TRUE, 'access content' => FALSE]);

// After:
use Drupal\user\Entity\Role;

Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->grantPermissions(['administer nodes'])->save();
Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->revokePermissions(['administer nodes'])->save();
Role::loadOverrideFree($rid)->changePermissions([
  'administer nodes' => TRUE,
  'access content' => FALSE,
])->save();

Note loadOverrideFree() can return NULL if the role doesn't exist, so guard with ?-> where appropriate, as done in media_install() and node_install().

Timeline

  • Opened: June 21, 2013
  • Committed: September 7, 2026 (13 years and 2 commits later)

The API shape was debated for years between andypost and alexpott: whether grantPermissions()/revokePermissions() should take an array argument or be variadic extensions of the singular methods, and whether the plural methods were even worth adding alongside the singular ones. alexpott argued a dedicated plural array-accepting method was clearer than overloading the singular method with variadic arguments, which andypost preferred for its type-safety of individual string arguments. When nicxvan picked up the implementation, they resolved the long-standing disagreement by following alexpott's array-based approach, and opened a follow-up (#3621087) to address the singular/plural question for UserCreationTrait separately. berdir's review noted the diff didn't change the actual list of permissions, only how the calls were made, and estimated contrib has roughly 700 call sites that would need similar conversion, suggesting Rector automation.

item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +446/−2 · php +417/−2 · yml +29

Summary

Entity view and form displays calculate their config dependencies from the widget and formatter plugins used on each field, so that deleting something a plugin depends on (a view mode, an image style, a taxonomy vocabulary, etc.) is blocked or handled safely. This calculation was broken whenever a display used the same plugin on more than one field: only the last field's dependencies were kept, so the others were silently dropped. A common trigger is two comment fields each set to show a different comment view mode, or two image fields using different image styles. If the missing dependency was later deleted, the display could break with a fatal error instead of being cleanly protected. Existing sites do not need to change anything, but should run database updates after upgrading so the new post update hooks can recalculate and fix the dependencies stored in their existing displays.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New field_post_update_recalculate_entity_form_display_dependencies() and field_post_update_recalculate_entity_view_display_dependencies() post update hooks resave all entity_form_display and entity_view_display config entities to recalculate their dependencies.

Technical details

EntityFormDisplay::getPluginCollections() and EntityViewDisplay::getPluginCollections() build a EntityDisplayPluginCollection keyed by $configuration['type'] (the plugin ID). When two fields on the same display use the same widget or formatter, the second field's configuration overwrote the first's in that array, so ConfigEntityBase::calculateDependencies(), which iterates the plugin collection to merge in each plugin's calculateDependencies() result, only ever saw one instance's dependencies. The fix rekeys both collections by $field_name instead of plugin type, which is guaranteed unique per display; calculateDependencies() never relied on the array keys, so this is safe.

Because existing config was calculated with the old, lossy keying, two new post update functions, field_post_update_recalculate_entity_form_display_dependencies() and field_post_update_recalculate_entity_view_display_dependencies(), use ConfigEntityUpdater to resave every entity_form_display and entity_view_display, forcing dependencies to be recalculated with the corrected code. Test coverage includes a new field_dynamic_dependencies_test module with a formatter/widget pair whose calculateDependencies() adds a configurable module dependency, used in EntityDisplayDependenciesTest to prove dependencies from multiple fields using the same plugin are all retained, plus RecalculateDependenciesUpdateTest to verify the update path against a pre-fix fixture.
